Réponse à coller sur la PR #452 (Marvisak/VIctory), en commentaire.
Branche poussée : merge de main 6c23321, limite 2^14 en cd6a864.

Thanks a lot for these measurements, the 2^20 / 2^16 / 2^14 comparison on the RTX 5070 makes the case clearly.

- The default general loop limit is now 2^14 (16,384) in cd6a864. The doc comment on `LOOP_LIMIT` gives the reason (the ~2 s host watchdog, your numbers) and the trade-off: a legitimate loop of more than 16,384 iterations per lane is cut short, so its result is wrong there.
- `VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT` still overrides it in every build, including release, so a higher value can check whether a wrong result comes from the limit. The spin-wait limit stays at 4096 and never above the loop limit, and the shader cache still keys on both.
- Current main (ffe310e) is merged in, no rebase (6c23321). In that main, `Lower` does not have `resolved_reads`, `pure_spill_writes` or `guard_slots` yet, and `Parts` has no `host_waves`, so those notes did not apply this time. The conflicts were in the test-only fields of `Lowered` and in the test helpers (main's `lower_wave` split and the new `resource::track` argument). I'll apply your notes when those PRs land.
- `cargo test -p victory-shader` passes on Linux: 102 tests (1 ignored). `cargo check --tests` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` passes for victory-shader, victory-gpu and victory.

Réponse à coller sur la PR #452, en réponse au commentaire de PastiiJay.

Thanks a lot for the RDNA4 numbers. Going from about 3.7 s per world frame with a device removal at around 60 s, to 0.58-0.97 s per frame and about 100 s in the world, matches what Nixitov saw: the long submissions were the roughly 2 s TDR, and the general loop limit keeps them under it. The page fault at the end is a separate issue, outside this PR.

Since your run, 3ede934 fixes the clippy failure on CI after the main merge. It changes no behaviour, so your numbers still hold. If you have time, a run with VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT=65536 would show whether 2^14 is lower than it needs to be.

Réponse à coller sur la PR #452, en réponse aux commentaires d'aycow.

Thanks for the careful report and the synthetic test, you were right. The classifier took returning buffer and image atomics as reads, so a counting loop at a fixed address could get the spin limit. Fixed in 5bcacf5: atomics now count as effects, like stores. The regression test `a_loop_of_returning_atomics_at_one_address_is_not` covers a returning `buffer_atomic_add` and an `image_atomic_add`, and it fails without the fix. A fixed-address load loop is still a spin wait (`a_loop_rereading_one_flag_is_a_spin_wait`). A rerun of your fixture on AMD, NVIDIA and WARP would be very welcome; it should now give 33 at limits 64/16.
